turns.thought:
Good catch — that "Data Disabled" flag is almost certainly your culprit. Picture messages (MMS) require an active mobile data connection; SMS (regular texts) rides on the voice/signaling channel, which is why your plain texts still go through while photos fail. Your signal (4 bars, 5G), APN/MMSC, and Wi‑Fi Calling all look fine, so let's start there.

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data ON**

Do one of these on your phone:
- Swipe down from the top of the screen **twice** to open the full Quick Settings panel, then tap the **Mobile data** (or "Cellular data") tile so it lights up / turns on.
- Or: **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → tap "Mobile data" to On.**

Once that's done:
- The status bar should now show a data icon alongside 5G (no more "Data Disabled").
- Please test it: turn off Wi‑Fi (already off) and open a web page in your browser to confirm data actually flows.
- Then try sending one picture message again and let me know if it goes through.

**Step 2 — If it still fails, grant the missing SMS permission**

You mentioned the messaging app has *storage* and *phone* but no *SMS* permission. That can also block picture messaging. To fix:
- **Settings → Apps → See all apps → messaging → Permissions → SMS → Allow.**
- If you don't see an "SMS" entry there, go to **Settings → Apps → Default apps → SMS app** and make sure **messaging** is selected as the default SMS app — that grants it the messaging permissions it needs.

Go ahead with Step 1 first and tell me what the status bar shows afterward and whether the photo message sends. If data turns on but the picture message still fails, we'll move to Step 2 and, if needed, escalate to our technical support team for a deeper look.

Mobile data being on is confirmed now (5G + Data Enabled), and your APN/MMSC, network type, and Wi‑Fi Calling all look correct, so the missing SMS permission on the messaging app is the most likely remaining cause. A picture message needs both the SMS and storage permissions to attach and hand off media.

**Step 2 — Grant the SMS permission**

- Open **Settings → Apps → See all apps → messaging → Permissions**.
- Find **SMS**. If it's listed, tap it and choose **Allow** (not "Ask every time" and not "Deny").
- Storage should already be **Allow** — leave it as is.

**Step 2b — If there's no "SMS" entry in that Permissions list**

Some phones only expose messaging permissions to the *default* SMS app, which is why you don't see it:
- Go to **Settings → Apps → Default apps → SMS app**.
- If **messaging** is not selected, select it. That grants it the messaging permissions it needs — you may get a confirmation prompt; accept it.
- Then go back into **messaging → Permissions** and confirm **SMS** now shows as allowed.

**After that — test again**

1. Send one picture message and check whether it goes through.
2. If it still fails, **reboot the phone** (hold the power button, then tap Restart). A reboot helps the permission and APN changes take effect — and it's also required after any APN reset we might do.

Let me know what you see after granting the permission and testing. If the app reports it still cannot send MMS after that, I'll pull in our technical support team to look at the line and messaging profile directly.
